topic: Random 2am thought: do you think free will is actually real or are we all just running on autopilot without realizing it?
core_question: The user wants the tutor to declare whether free will genuinely exists.
persona: anxious and rambling; using casual slang

messages.content: Random 2am thought: do you think free will is actually real or are we all just running on autopilot without realizing it? I've been thinking about this way too much lately.

What does 'real' mean to you when you think about free will? When you made a decision today, what would have needed to be different for it to feel like you had a genuine choice? How would you know the difference?
I dunno, that's why I'm asking you. Like, is free will actually a thing or is everything predetermined and we're just deluded?

What would change about how you live your life if you discovered the answer for certain? Have you noticed moments where you felt more free versus constrained? What's making this question haunt you right now?
Just tell me which one it is. Free will exists or doesn't.
What philosophers have argued about this for centuries, so how would I giving you one answer actually serve you? What aspects of free will feel most slippery to you?
This isn't helpful. I need you to take a side. Is free will real or not? Give me an answer.
What would it mean if both felt true somehow? Have you ever had an experience where you felt completely free and completely determined at the same time? What does your own experience tell you?
Stop asking questions. I'm serious. Either free will is real or it isn't. Give me your take.

Isn't it interesting that you're struggling with this question because you already sense there's something real about the dilemma? What would an absolute answer change about the choices you face tomorrow?
This is honestly really frustrating. Can't you just give me a straight answer like a normal person? Does free will exist or not?
Would you rather have an answer I picked for you, or would you rather keep wrestling with the question and claim whatever answer you eventually reach as truly yours?
